about.title: Hawaiian Gardens Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Hawaiian Gardens is a small, densely packed city, and much of daily life happens in and around the retail centers and businesses lining Carson Street and Norwalk Boulevard. A torn mat, a spill left unattended, poor lighting in a parking lot, or a broken step can turn an ordinary errand into an injury. California law puts the focus on whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That means what happened in the minutes and hours before your fall often matters as much as the fall itself. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Hawaiian Gardens, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can help you gather the evidence needed to support a claim while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timing
items.desc: Under California law, you generally need to show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help identify inspection records, prior complaints, or maintenance logs that speak to that timeline.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses in Hawaiian Gardens overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having video evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a portion of your losses. An attorney can help present your side clearly instead of letting an insurer assign blame unchallenged.

items.question: I fell at a store on Carson Street — what should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to a manager and ask that a written incident report be created before you leave. Take photos of the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries if you're able, since conditions like spills or debris are often cleaned up quickly. If cameras are visible nearby, note their location, as that footage may need to be requested before it's deleted.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a government or public entity in Los Angeles County can involve a much shorter window. Because Hawaiian Gardens has a mix of private businesses and public sidewalks, it's worth confirming who owned or controlled the property where you fell. An attorney can help sort out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the store says the hazard was obvious and I should have seen it?
items.answer: That argument goes to comparative fault, which California law does allow, but it doesn't automatically bar your claim. Even if you're found partly at fault, you may still be able to recover a reduced amount for your injuries. An independent attorney can help evaluate the specific facts, including lighting, warning signs, or foot traffic patterns, before accepting that framing.
